problem: Social navigation prior work is myopic, treats pedestrian forecasts as fixed inputs independent of robot actions, or couples prediction and planning through expensive optimization. Latent world models used in RL compress away spatial structure and only loosely feed foresight to the policy.
motivation: Robot and human motions are mutually coupled, so a robot has to reason about how the scene and pedestrians evolve under each candidate action. Existing imagination-based RL either accumulates compounding errors (pure imagination) or leaves prediction and planning decoupled (representation or reward augmentation only).
key_idea: Train an action-conditioned world model in Depth Anything V2 patch-feature space with depth and human-trajectory decoders, and inject its imagined futures into a DD-PPO policy by fusing per-action future features into the observation embedding and shaping rewards from predicted human trajectories.
insight: Foresight helps most when it is injected into the policy. Fusing action-conditioned future features lifts single-robot SR from 43.36 to 55.87 and multi-robot SR from 13.64 to 28.52, and trajectory reward shaping adds a further 3.6 SR and 5.6 SPL in single-robot. The decoders also improve the world model itself: adding depth then trajectory losses raises latent CosSim from 0.9278 to 0.9383 and lowers depth RMSE from 0.0406 to 0.0371.
method: Observation model: a frozen Depth Anything V2 ViT encodes the depth image into patch embeddings z_t (P x D), which keeps spatial structure and generalises across scenes.

Transition model: a block-causal ViT Transformer with a sliding window of length H. It takes patch tokens plus one action token per frame and autoregressively predicts next-frame patch features, trained with an L2 latent consistency loss.

Decoder heads: a DPT-style depth decoder, a trajectory decoder and a reward MLP (the last two on mean-pooled features), trained with task losses independently of the transition model, to anchor latents to geometry and human motion.
Observation encoder: a ResNet on depth, concatenated with the previous action and passed through a GRU, gives the embedding e_t.

Imagination module (action-conditioned future-feature fusion): queries the transition model for every candidate action (Forward, Turn-Left, Turn-Right, Stop), concatenates the predicted latents into l_t, and fuses them with e_t in a detached late fusion before the actor-critic.
Social reward shaping: reward is goal progress plus success bonus, minus collision penalty, minus a predictive social cost r_traj computed from the world model's forecast human trajectories.
Policy training: on-policy DD-PPO with discrete actions, with the policy grounded in real observations rather than trained purely in imagination.

setting.backbone: Frozen DA-V2 ViT encoder + causal Transformer world model + ResNet/GRU actor-critic policy (DD-PPO), trained from scratch apart from the frozen DA-V2
setting.training_data: Trained on Social-HM3D episodes via on-policy RL with a replay buffer for the world model; no extra web or synthetic data. Social-MP3D is zero-shot.
setting.observation: egocentric depth image + goal + robot pose (previous action)
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT human trajectories and depth are used only as world-model training supervision)

numbers.backbone: DA-V2 world model + ResNet-GRU DD-PPO policy

results: NavThinker reaches SR 59.46 / SPL 55.00 on single-robot Social-HM3D, beating the strongest baseline Falcon (56.26 / 52.05) with fewer human collisions (39.09 vs 41.22). It also beats Falcon on multi-robot Social-HM3D (SR 30.04 vs 28.63). On zero-shot Social-MP3D it trails Falcon in SR (47.33 vs 51.67) but has the lowest H-Coll.
limitations: Uses depth only, with no RGB or semantic input, and imagines only one step ahead, so longer horizons for complex interactions are left open.
Zero-shot Social-MP3D success (47.33) is below Falcon (51.67), and real-world evidence is only qualitative.
Baselines are limited to A*, ORCA, Habitat-official and Falcon, and results are reported as single runs with no variance.
